description: Glossia canonical test vectors. Two invariants: (1) decode(encode(x)) == x (round-trip), (2) decode(frozen_prose) == expected (backward compat). Decode stability vectors are append-only and must never be edited or removed.

round_trip_vectors.description: One 0x00 byte — minimal payload, tests zero-value preservation
Three bytes — odd byte count, tests non-word-aligned packing
Leading zeros must survive round-trip — not silently dropped
16 zero bytes — worst case for leading-zero preservation
16 bytes of 0xFF — exercises high-index wordlist entries
32-byte pseudo-random blob — longer payload stress test

A bare 12-word BIP39 mnemonic given to the 'encode' verb is treated as raw data (text), not silently transcoded as a seed, so it round-trips verbatim. The verb is authoritative: to re-encode a mnemonic as a seed (compacting it into a denser language) use the 'transcode' verb (e.g. 'transcode into latin', which auto-detects the source) or name the source explicitly ('transcode from english/bip39/raw into latin').

error_vectors.description: Prose with no payload words must fail to decode
error_vectors.input_prose: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

codec_vectors.description: Bitpack: 1 byte with 2048 words → padding word index = number of padding bits
codec_vectors.note: 8 data bits, ceil(8/11)=1 data word, pad=11-8=3

codec_vectors.description: Bitpack: 1 byte with 16 words (4 bits/word) → zero padding bits
codec_vectors.note: 8 bits / 4 bits_per_word = 2 data words, no padding

codec_vectors.description: Base-N: leading zero bytes must round-trip with non-power-of-2 wordlist

merkle_vectors.description: parse_merkleized(merkleize(words)) must recover original words in order
Minimal Merkle tree: 2 payload, 1 cover — root is always a cover word

dialect_detection_vectors._comment: Dialect detection: given encoded prose, detect_dialect() must rank the correct language/wordlist first. The invariant is: prose encoded with language L and wordlist W must detect as L/W. Detection uses unique input words, so repeated words (e.g., 'abandon' x11) count once.
